Here’s a quick‑look guide to some of the most compelling **crime‑thrillers released (or widely available) in 2020**—the ones critics praised, audiences loved, and binge‑watchers can’t stop talking about:

| # | Title & Year | Director(s) | Key Cast | Streaming / Release Notes | Why It Stands Out |
|---|--------------|-------------|----------|---------------------------|------------------|
| 1 | *Tenet* (2019/2020)* | Christopher Nolan | John David Washington, Robert Pattinson, Elizabeth Debicki | Netflix (US), theatrical worldwide | A mind‑bending heist thriller where time itself becomes an ally—and enemy. Nolan’s signature non‑linear storytelling keeps you guessing until the very end. |
| 2 | *Uncut Gems* (2019/2020)** | Josh Safdie, Benny Safdie | Adam Sandler, Kevin Garnett, Jennifer Lawrence | Amazon Prime Video (U.S.) | An adrenaline‑packed New York City story featuring Sandler as a high‑stakes jeweler whose greed spirals into chaos. The film’s frenetic pacing mirrors its protagonist’s frantic life. |
| 3 | *The Gentlemen* (2019/2020)** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Michelle Dockery | Hulu (UK), HBO Max (USA) | Ritchie's slick blend of British gangster tropes and sharp humor delivers a stylish caper full of twists and witty dialogue. |
| 4 | *Nobody* (2021 but filmed 2020) | Ilya Naishuller | Bob Odenkirk, J.K. Simmons, Nicky Kinnaird | Paramount+ (U.S.), theatrical worldwide | Though officially a 2021 release, production wrapped in late 2020. Odenkirk turns his “Drunk Driver” persona into a surprisingly brutal vigilante action‑thief saga. |
| 5 | *The Irishman* (2019/2020)** | Martin Scorsese | Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci | Netflix (global) | While technically a biographical crime epic, its intricate plotlines and masterful use of de-aging tech make it feel like a modern crime‑thriller masterpiece. |
| 6 | *Mortal Kombat: Legacy* (2020) – TV series | Various | Tessa Thompson, Michael B. Jordan | Peacock (U.S.) | Not strictly a movie, but this serialized take on the classic fighting game blends martial arts choreography with gritty underworld intrigue—a fresh spin on the genre. |

\* *Tenet* premiered in December 2019; many U.S. viewers first saw it on Netflix in early 2020 after limited theatrical runs were cut short due to COVID‑19.  
\*\* Films shot during 2020 may have had delayed releases or distribution changes because of pandemic restrictions.

---

### Quick Picks If You’re Short On Time

| Film | One‑Line Hook |
|------|---------------|
| *Tenet* | "A spy who manipulates time to prevent World War III." |
| *Uncut Gems* | "An eccentric jeweller's gamble goes wildly wrong." |
| *The Gentlemen* | "British gangsters swap turf while keeping secrets tight." |
| *Nobody* | "Every day is ordinary… until one night." |
| *The Irishman* | "Revisiting decades of mob history through a single man’s eyes." |

> **Tip:** For those looking specifically for *movies* rather than miniseries or documentaries, focus on the first five entries above—they all hit theaters (albeit sometimes briefly) before moving onto major streaming platforms.

Enjoy your cinematic dive into crime, suspense, and unexpected twists!
